title: Exponential of a linear map in the Gaussian polynomial closure
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $1\le p<\infty$, let $L\colon\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb C$ be a continuous real-linear map, and let $f$ belong to the complex-valued $L^p$ space for product standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. If $f(x)=\exp(L(x))$ for Gaussian-almost every $x$, then $f$ lies in the $L^p$ closure of the set of functions represented by complex polynomials in the coordinates on $\mathbb R^n$.
hypotheses_covered: $L\colon\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb C$ is continuous and real-linear
$f$ belongs to complex-valued $L^p$ for product standard Gaussian measure
$f(x)=\exp(L(x))$ almost everywhere for product standard Gaussian measure
